confidence_notes: I ran three web searches: one for the RBA rate and two for Uyuni and Bolivia prices. Food and drink anchors come from travel-cost aggregators and Bolivia-wide cost-of-living sites. These disagree by a few tenths of a dollar, and some are dated. Uyuni-specific figures were thin. Beer is set near the Uyuni-listed pint of about $2.6 and the national $1.9-2.3 range, with a tourist-town premium. Coffee is set between the national figure of about $2.5 and Uyuni listings of $1.5-2.4. The inexpensive meal and mid-range two-person meal are scaled from Uyuni and Bolivia figures, with a tourist-restaurant premium. I found no reliable cocktail or wine-by-the-glass prices. Cocktail is about 2x beer and wine glass about 1.7x beer, a relationship assumed from general knowledge of Bolivian tourist venues. Accommodation anchors are holistic estimates from general knowledge of Uyuni as a salt-flat tour hub with limited, seasonal supply. I did not search for accommodation or inspect any listings.
comparable_city_reasoning: Based on Bolivian tourist-town price levels (Sucre and La Paz tourist areas), with a modest premium for Uyuni's remote location and tour-driven demand.
